notes: VmRSS, VmHWM and VmSwap are exact /proc/<pid>/status fields in kB.
DRM values retain their exact fdinfo field names and units; duplicate client IDs per device are sampled once.
Field type or unit changes are retained as separate observations; maxima are compared only within the same unit.
DRM client maxima can occur at different times; do not add maxima or combine them with RSS as a total or shared GPU peak.
CPU seconds cover the first through last successful sample, excluding earlier process work.
Process count fields retain exact stat/status names; status context-switch counts describe the main thread. Compare cumulative counters only within the same PID/start identity.
Full rows stream to the optional trace; observer memory retains per-process/client maxima and first/last counters rather than sample history.

trace.timestamp_clock: time.monotonic; sampled after process and optional system reads
trace.scheduling_scope: Per-task schedstat sums. Runtime and runqueue wait use ns; timeslices and read_errors are counts. Compare deltas only with identical task_ids and no read errors.
trace.capture_scope: Capture elapsed covers process/system reads before aggregation and trace output. Previous-sample gaps also include trace write time and the requested interval; they do not identify scheduling delays alone.

system_sampling.scope: Host sysfs/proc/statvfs snapshots. Meminfo preserves kB; vmstat fields are separate cumulative kernel counters, not interchangeable units. PSI totals use microseconds and averages use percent. Scratch free includes reserved blocks; available excludes them. RAPL is cumulative energy with a wrap range, not power. Throttle counters can be duplicated across CPU siblings. Missing/denied fields are omitted and counted as errors, never zero-filled.
